text_blocks.snippet: Gilbert's syndrome is a common, harmless, and usually symptom-free genetic condition where the liver doesn't process bilirubin (a waste product from red blood cell breakdown) as efficiently as it should. This leads to mild jaundice (yellowing of the skin and eyes) and, in some cases, fatigue. It's typically diagnosed in adolescence or early adulthood and doesn't require treatment.
snippet_highlighted_words: a common, harmless, and usually symptom-free genetic condition where the liver doesn't process bilirubin (a waste product from red blood cell breakdown) as efficiently as it should
